name: HVAC/R Technology
description: HVAC/R programmes train the people who install, service and repair heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration systems — in a state where air conditioning is not a comfort but the thing that makes buildings usable. ⚠ It is electrical work, mechanical work and refrigerant handling at once, and the last of those is federally regulated.
degreesNote: Florida's framework is a 1,350-hour clock-hour certificate with five occupational completion points, and ⚠ it is also published as two halves — a 750-hour first part and a 600-hour second — so a student can finish the first, go to work, and return. Several state colleges run a college-credit version instead, and a few add an associate degree or an advanced technical certificate above it. ⚠⚠ Certification is separate from the certificate and is not optional: EPA Section 608 is required by federal law to work on equipment containing refrigerant. ⚠⚠⚠ And unlike welding or automotive, the trade above this one is LICENSED — Florida licenses air-conditioning contractors through the Construction Industry Licensing Board (Class A unlimited, Class B up to 25 tons of cooling), so the career has a statutory ceiling that only a licence lifts.

cips.note: ⚠ Where Florida actually files HVAC: 45 public institutions and 891 credentials in 2023. The state's own frameworks — the 1,350-hour certificate and both halves — are filed here, under engineering technology rather than under maintenance.

HVAC maintenance technology — 31 institutions and 111 credentials. ⚠ Included because it is the other code Florida institutions use for the same training, and a student searching one would miss the other.

related.note: ⚠ The step up: an associate degree in engineering or building-systems technology leads to design, controls, energy management and the contractor's licence route — which is where the money stops being hourly.
The other large clock-hour trade at the same technical colleges. ⚠ Sheet-metal and pipe skills overlap enough that some HVAC technicians add a welding certificate for commercial and industrial work.
